transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes

Summary: High-level posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts, how ACME Health can access the Trust Center, mapping of ACME controls to Redwood evidence, questions about RBAC/SSO/SAML, audit logs retention, and KMS key management. Action items and a follow-up technical deep dive on KMS/VPC networking were agreed.

Topics: Trust Center access, reports (SOC2/ISO), controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, KMS/E2E encryption, data residency, evidence collection cadence.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
00:06 Priya (ACME Security): Priya here. Hi.
00:08 Dan (ACME Infra): Dan.
00:09 Leah (ACME Legal): Leah on.
00:11 Alex: Great. From Redwood: Samira and Miguel are on to cover technical and compliance details. Samira, you want to kick?
00:20 Samira (Redwood SE): Sure, thanks. I'll do an overview of where our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts live and then we can walk through your control mapping questions. Quick note, the recording might have some auto-transcript quirks, so apologies if names get spelled odd.
00:36 Priya: That's fine. Our ask up front — we need to understand what exact scope was in your last SOC 2 Type II, how often you rotate keys, where customer data at rest lives, and whether we can get mapping to ACME controls for our own audit.
00:52 Miguel (Redwood Security PM): Absolutely. Short answer: our SOC 2 Type II (last 12-month window) and ISO 27001 certificate are available in the Trust Center. We provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report for customers under NDA. For high-level, the scope covers hosted API, dedicated pools, and control plane components — not on-prem customer-managed packages.
01:12 Leah: When you say "Trust Center," is that a portal we can log into and pull artifacts, or is it emailed on request? We need to know the access flow for legal/compliance to download artifacts.
01:25 Alex: Good question. We have a Trust Center portal (link: https://trust.redwood.com) — customers that sign an NDA are given scoped access; there is a request workflow. We'll provide a short access guide.
01:39 Dan: Is there an SSO integration for that portal? We prefer SAML with our IdP (Okta).
01:44 Samira: Yes, the Trust Center supports SAML/SSO — you can tie it to Okta and enforce RBAC for who can view reports. The main platform also supports SAML-based SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.
01:58 Priya: On RBAC, can we map roles to least privilege? We want separation: billing vs dev ops vs security.
02:07 Miguel: RBAC is role-based and configurable. We expose several built-in roles and you can create custom roles; audit logs capture role changes and privilege escalations. Retention for admin audit events is 12 months in the hosted default, longer retention is an add-on.
02:22 Priya: Follow up: is that 12 months immutable? We need tamper-evidence for certain logs for compliance.
02:29 Miguel: Tamper-evidence is provided via WORM for selected audit log exports and an append-only audit trail in the control plane. For customers requiring long-term immutable retention we recommend pushing exports to their own S3 bucket (VPC endpoint) — that gives them full control.
02:45 Dan: Do you provide a CloudTrail-style export for all API calls? We have to ingest it into our SIEM.
02:51 Samira: We provide both near-real-time webhook/event streaming and periodic export bundles. The audit events include API calls, admin console changes, role assignments, and authentication events. We also have a connector that streams to customers' S3 and supports delivery to SIEMs.
03:12 Leah: About encryption — what keys are used for customer data at rest? Do you BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with HSM/KMS?
03:20 Miguel: We support two models: Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or equivalent in other clouds. With CMK, you hold key policy controls and can rotate/disable keys; Redwood performs envelope encryption and we never have access to plaintext without the key. For on-prem/private installs, we support HSM integrations.
03:42 Priya: Do you do application-level encryption for embeddings and derived artifacts or only block-level disk encryption? We are worried about model outputs and embeddings persisting.
03:51 Samira: We encrypt at multiple layers: disk-level encryption, database column encryption for sensitive indexes, and application-layer envelope encryption for cached KV and embedding stores. Embedding caching is optional and can be disabled per customer.
04:10 Priya: Good. For SOC 2 mapping — we have a controls matrix we need Redwood to fill out showing which of our controls map to Redwood's controls. What's your process?
04:18 Miguel: We usually start with a controls mapping template (you can use your template or ours). We'll fill in which controls we cover, provide evidence pointers (e.g., audit log exports, policy docs, penetration test reports). Note that some items will be shared responsibility, like customer application-level access controls.
04:37 Alex: We'll ask for your template after the call. Miguel, can you outline what evidence types are typically available?
04:43 Miguel: Sure: redacted SOC2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, third-party pen-test summary (full reports under NDA), system architecture diagrams, policy docs (incident response, change management), sample audit log exports, encryption architecture, and control implementation notes. The Trust Center has those artifacts organized per control family.
05:05 Dan: About data residency — our workloads must keep data in the eu-west-1 region and records stored in eu only. Do you support region pinning for hosted inference?
05:15 Samira: Yes, we support region-specific deployments; customers can pin workloads to a region and we can configure data residency — there is an extra configuration step and a dedicated regional tenancy option for stronger isolation.
05:29 Priya: What's the process for attestation that data never leaves region X? Is that something in the SLA or a separate compliance attestation?
05:37 Miguel: We provide configuration-level guarantees and logs showing endpoints and node placement. For contractual attestation we can add a data residency addendum and provide periodic reports. For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.
05:56 Leah: On legal — what does your DPA say about subprocessors? We need the subprocessors list and notification cadence.
06:05 Alex: We maintain a subprocessors register in the Trust Center and push notifications for major changes. The DPA is available to sign; we can share a redline-friendly copy.
06:15 Leah: Perfect.
06:17 Priya: A couple of nitty-gritty things — what is your vulnerability management cadence? CVE triage windows?
06:24 Miguel: We run continuous scanning, weekly triage for critical/important CVEs, and a quarterly pentest. Critical issues are patched in accordance with severity SLAs; we also publish a monthly security bulletin in the Trust Center.
06:39 Dan: Backups: what are your backup encryption and retention policies? We need restoration test proofs.
06:45 Samira: Backups are encrypted with CMKs or Redwood-managed keys, snapshots are retained per-customer retention settings — default 30 days, extendable. We run quarterly restore drills for core systems and can provide summary evidence.
07:03 Priya: On identity: do you support SCIM for provisioning so we can automate Deprovisioning?
07:08 Miguel: Yes, SCIM is supported for provisioning and sync with Okta/Azure AD. Combined with SSO we can automate provisioning flows; deprovisioning events are captured in audit logs.
07:21 Alex: We sometimes get questions about independence of audit — who performed your SOC 2 audit?
07:26 Miguel: It was audited by GrayWave Partners (third-party CPA firm). We'll include the auditor name in the artifact.
07:33 Priya: Can you confirm the scope boundaries again — is Dedicated included or is it a separate report?
07:38 Samira: Dedicated pools are included if they are hosted and managed by Redwood. Private on-prem installs are covered by a separate attestation model; for Private deployments we provide posture documentation but the SOC 2 report focuses on Redwood-managed services.
07:54 Priya: We might need a signed controls mapping for our ISO alignment — would Redwood sign a mapping that says "control X is handled by Redwood"?
08:03 Miguel: We can sign a responsibility matrix or provide a formal controls letter as part of enterprise contracts. We'll need to align on scoping and exact language; legal is usually involved.
08:15 Leah: That sounds reasonable; we'll scope the list and get back.
08:20 Dan: One last technical — how do you handle KV cache persistence? If an adversary compromised a node, what's the exposure?
08:27 Samira: The KV cache uses envelope encryption with CMK or Redwood-managed key, and nodes are ephemeral. Persistent caches are stored in encrypted object storage with restricted network access. If a node is compromised, cached plaintext exposure is mitigated by short TTLs and we scrub caches on redeploy. For high-security customers we recommended disabling server-side caching and using client-side or customer-managed cache.
08:55 Priya: Good to know.
08:58 Alex: Ok let's recap next steps — Alex will share the Trust Center link and SOC 2 redacted report under NDA, Samira to schedule the KMS/VPC technical deep dive, Priya to send the control mapping template. Leah to review DPA redline timeline. Anything else?
09:15 Leah: Can you also include a brief on audit log schema so our SIEM team can map fields?
09:21 Samira: Yes, we'll include the event schema and sample export.
09:25 Priya: Also, pen-test executive summary please.
09:29 Miguel: We'll include the executive summary; full reports require NDA.
09:33 Alex: Great — we'll follow up via email with links and schedule. Thanks everyone.
